record.question:
A company will run CRM microservices as separate Amazon ECS tasks on EC2. Each microservice needs its own security groups and network-flow visibility, and must receive only the AWS API permissions it requires. Long-lived access keys must not be distributed to containers.

Which task configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Use bridge networking with a narrowly scoped task IAM role for each microservice. Apply the network security groups to the shared container instances.
Use awsvpc networking and task security groups. Put all application permissions in the task execution role and omit the task IAM role.
Use awsvpc networking and task security groups. Inject a narrowly scoped IAM user access key into each container at launch.
Use awsvpc networking with security groups on each task ENI. Assign a narrowly scoped task IAM role to each microservice and use its temporary credentials for application API calls.

explanation.text:
<<4>> is correct. `awsvpc` gives each task a network interface to which security groups apply and from which VPC Flow Logs can be collected. A task IAM role supplies application permissions independently of the EC2 container instance role, without distributing long-lived keys.

<<1>> scopes API access correctly but keeps network controls at the shared host interface rather than providing each task's required network boundary.

<<2>> confuses two roles. The execution role authorizes ECS startup activities such as pulling images and retrieving injected secrets; it is not the application's task role.

<<3>> meets the network requirement but violates the prohibition on long-lived access keys.

These controls are per task. Containers within one task share its network stack and task role. On EC2, task roles and networking do not create a complete isolation boundary from a compromised host or colocated containers; host and instance-metadata protections still matter.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [ECS task networking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-networking-awsvpc.html). [ECS task IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.html).

diagram_alt: A task ENI controls network access while a separate task role scopes application API permissions.

sources.supports: Per-task ENI, security groups, VPC Flow Logs, and shared networking within a task
Application credentials, execution-role distinction, and EC2 container isolation limits

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 4. Replaced ambiguous container-level isolation with separate-task requirements and distinguished task, execution, and instance roles.
